from.place: the constructible variant clause and its bounded flat constructible model

title: Etale bounded flat constructible model
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring, let X be a Noetherian scheme, and let a b : ℤ with an explicit hypothesis hab : a ≤ b. For every bounded constructible object K of the derived category of sheaves of Λ-modules on the small etale site of X, K has Tor amplitude in [a,b] if and only if there exists a cochain complex P of such sheaves that is flat and constructible termwise, zero outside [a,b], and whose image in the derived category is isomorphic to K. The site and sheaf categories use [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and Tor amplitude is the derived-category Tor-amplitude notion in the cited declaration. Here bounded constructible means $H^n(K)=0$ for all but finitely many $n$, with each $H^n(K)$ constructible in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. The derived category and its localization $Q$ are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ means $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F[0])=0$ for every sheaf $F$ and every $i<a$ or $i>b$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude; def-kun-derived-tensor]. Flat means that tensoring with the sheaf is exact; zero outside $[a,b]$ means every such term is a zero object. All sheaves use the ModuleCat encoding of $\Lambda$-module sheaves.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] on each $H^n(K)$ to convert the finite-value constructibility hypothesis to the source $\operatorname{IsConstructibleSheaf}$ predicate. The category and sheaves are unchanged. Let $T$ be this source constructibility property and $S(F)$ mean $T(F)$ and flatness of $F$.

source.place: hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel, lines 160-214; constructible variant of blueprint lem-sf-flat-model

proof.text: The kernel and cokernel clauses of [thm-constructible-serre], together with the comparison [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] on source, target and resulting object, show that $T$ is closed under kernels and cokernels. Thus this applies to maps whose terms satisfy the source predicate, not merely to terms given in the finite-value encoding.

source.place: hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel, lines 160-214; constructible variant of blueprint lem-sf-flat-model

proof.text: The zero sheaf is constant with zero module value on the one-stratum partition of $X$, so it is constructible. An isomorphism preserves a trivialization on every stratum, so $T$ is invariant under isomorphism. Flatness is invariant under isomorphism by conjugating the exact tensor functors, and tensor with zero is the zero exact functor. For $F,G$ in $S$, the split exact sequence $0\to F\to F\oplus G\to G\to0$ and [thm-constructible-serre] give constructibility of $F\oplus G$, after applying the comparison to both ends and back to the middle. The binary case of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct] gives its flatness, since the biproduct is the binary coproduct. Hence $S$ contains zero, is invariant under isomorphisms and is closed under binary biproducts; $S\subseteq T$ and $S\subseteq\mathrm{Flat}$ hold by definition.

source.place: hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel, lines 160-214; constructible variant of blueprint lem-sf-flat-model

proof.text: For every epimorphism $p:A\to B$ and map $g:G\to B$ with $T(G)$, [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible-lifting] produces $E$ in $S$, an epimorphism $e:E\to G$ and $h:E\to A$ satisfying $p\circ h=g\circ e$. This is exactly the lifting hypothesis for the class-resolution theorem; it does not assert that the constructible sheaf $G$ itself is flat or projective.

source.place: hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel, lines 160-214; constructible variant of blueprint lem-sf-flat-model

proof.text: Suppose $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sf-flat-model-class-resolution] to the category of small-etale $\Lambda$-module sheaves and the classes $S,T$ just checked. Every $H^n(K)$ belongs to $T$ by step 1. The amplitude test is literally the vanishing required in that theorem; the source's t-structure version is the same two inequalities $i<a$ and $i>b$. It gives $P$ supported in $[a,b]$, flat with every term in $T$, and $Q(P)\cong K$. Invert that isomorphism and apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] separately to each $P^n$. The terms then have exactly the finite-value constructibility requested in the item. In the source resolution, the good truncation term is a cokernel in $T$; no hard truncation at $b$ or change to an arbitrary representative is used.

source.place: hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel, lines 160-214; constructible variant of blueprint lem-sf-flat-model

proof.text: Conversely, suppose such a $P$ and $K\cong Q(P)$ exist. Discard only the additional termwise constructibility assertion and use the reverse direction of [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] with the same $\Lambda,X,a,b$, the stated $a\le b$, and the given bounded-constructible $K$ (converted by the comparison as in step 1). It yields Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for $K$. This converse does not assume or claim that every bounded-constructible object has finite Tor amplitude.
